data.description:
## Description
**What**: Build the walking-skeleton path: a shared normalize-and-sort registry library, a plugin-shipped seed registry of artifact-reference pairs, and a bootstrap migration script that fans out ast-grep over chunked codebase slices (map) and equijoins per-file tuples on the realpath-normalized path (reduce) to emit admitted writer/reference pairs.
**Why**: Without a deterministic discovered registry there is nothing for the Category 8 reviewer pass or the refresh command to consume; this is the minimal 'pairs discovered into a registry' spine.
**Scope**:
- IN: shared normalize-and-sort library file sourced by the bootstrap; seed registry YAML shipping the three named pairs; bootstrap map/reduce script using long-form ast-grep; write-idiom vocabulary (shell >/>>, tee, sed -i, jq write, Python open(w)/Path.write_text, Node fs.writeFileSync, Ruby File.open(w)/File.write, Go os.WriteFile) externally extensible via registry config; admission rule (exact realpath match + recognized write idiom + writer and reference in different files).
- OUT: refresh command (draft-3); reviewer consumption (draft-5); ambiguous/inferred pairs.

## Done Definitions

- The plugin-shipped seed registry contains the pair release.sh paired with marketplace.json ← Validates Closure Check: "The plugin-shipped seed registry contains the pairs release.sh<->marketplace.json, *.conf<->CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md, and plugin.json<->marketplace source ref."
- The plugin-shipped seed registry contains the pair *.conf paired with CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md and the pair plugin.json paired with the marketplace source ref ← Validates Closure Check: "The plugin-shipped seed registry contains the pairs release.sh<->marketplace.json, *.conf<->CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md, and plugin.json<->marketplace source ref."
- The shared normalize-and-sort registry library file exists and the bootstrap script sources it ← Validates Closure Check: "The shared normalize-and-sort registry library file exists and is sourced by both the bootstrap and refresh scripts."
- Running the bootstrap over a fixture repo emits output byte-equal to a sorted newline-delimited writer_realpath<TAB>reference_realpath manifest with no missing or extra rows; near-miss fixtures (same-file self-reference; cross-file read-only) are absent from the output ← Satisfies: sc-3
- Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic including the realpath-normalized equijoin, write-idiom recognition, and near-miss rejection ← Satisfies: sc-3

## Considerations

- [Build] New .sh files set the executable bit (chmod +x) on creation; the test gate and pre-commit hooks skip non-executable .sh files.
- [Correctness] All ast-grep invocations use the long-form ast-grep binary, never the bare sg alias, to avoid the shadow-utils collision.
- [Risk] Bootstrap sub-agents can truncate tuple lists at context limit silently; emit a per-slice count and fail the reduce when a slice returns no tuples unexpectedly.
- [Determinism] The shared library performs idempotent sort-dedup so bootstrap and refresh share identical normalization.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a DSO maintainer, I want a bootstrap migration that discovers writer/reference artifact pairs into a seed registry, so that planning has an authoritative coupling list.
